title: DeepSeek Clarifies Overtime Pay Calculation Rules, Mid-Autumn and National Day Holidays Bring a Ten-Day Half-Price Window

content_html:
On September 19, DeepSeek officially released a supplementary explanation regarding API peak and off-peak hours, clearly stating that weekends with adjusted workdays and national holidays in China are all billed at off-peak rates. This means that developers can enjoy off-peak pricing when calling APIs on September 20 (Sunday with adjusted workday), October 10 (Saturday with adjusted workday), and during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays.

According to DeepSeek's previously announced peak and off-peak pricing mechanism, the peak hours on weekdays (9:00-12:00, 14:00-18:00) are twice as expensive as the off-peak hours, while the entire weekend is uniformly billed at the off-peak rate. This supplementary explanation further clarifies the ambiguity of whether "adjusted workdays" are considered weekdays or weekends, explicitly stating that any weekend will be charged at the off-peak rate.

According to this rule, from September 20 to October 10, DeepSeek will experience an extended promotional period: three days of the Mid-Autumn Festival (September 25-27), seven days of National Day (October 1-7), plus two adjusted weekend days, totaling more than ten days all billed at off-peak hours, making it the most concentrated period of "half-price days" of the year.

At the same time, DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash model, released on September 10, further improves the cost-effectiveness. This 552B parameter MoE model uses an asymmetric architecture, activating only 8B parameters for input and 16B parameters for output, yet outperforms its flagship V4Pro model in multiple benchmark tests, while being priced at the Flash tier. During off-peak hours, the input cache hit rate for V4.1 Flash is as low as 0.02 yuan per million Tokens, and the output is only 4 yuan per million Tokens.
